scenario_text: A small mass hangs from a spring and oscillates vertically while moving through a viscous surrounding medium that resists its motion. The medium provides a retarding force proportional to speed, gradually removing energy from the motion. Starting from an initial displacement and velocity, the position evolves over time. The behavior depends on the spring stiffness, the mass, and the damping strength.

(2) -(beta/m)*x**3 is the Duffing cubic stiffness term, well-known. (3) -(gamma/m)*x**2*v is a van der Pol type nonlinear damping term, a recognized classical form. (4) -(c_q/m)*v*Abs(v) is standard quadratic/form-drag, textbook. (5) -(c/m)*(F_h/c)*(1-exp(-t/tau_h)) simplifies to -(F_h/m)*(1-exp(-t/tau_h)), an exponentially saturating time-dependent bias forcing term — this is an unusual composite forcing. (6) -(c_history/m)*z coupled with the auxiliary state z evolving via -z/tau_h - v/tau_h represents a first-order relaxation approximation of Basset history drag — a nontrivial memory-kernel construction. (7) -(c_shear/m)*v/(1+(v/v_ref)**2) is a shear-thinning velocity-dependent damping with a rational saturation, an uncommon composite term. While individually several terms (Duffing, van der Pol, quadratic drag) are known classical additions, the COMPLETE combined form — integrating an exponentially-relaxing bias force, a first-order memory-state approximation of history drag with its own auxiliary ODE, and a rational shear-thinning damping term — does not correspond to any single textbook or standard published equation. No LLM could recite this exact combined form from the context alone; the specific composite structure (particularly the shear-thinning rational term and the history-drag relaxation coupling) could only be identified through data-driven inference. Therefore the assembled equation constitutes a genuinely novel composite model even though its constituent motifs draw on known physics.
